key_insight: The paper proposes a single doubly-spectral stochastic (DSS) representation for graph neural networks that unifies calibration, OOD detection, and robustness by separating structural and latent uncertainty in one model.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners one uncertainty-aware GNN framework that can be deployed either standalone or as a residual hybrid to improve reliability without changing the core prediction pipeline.
method: Represent node embeddings as random graph signals with graph Fourier coefficients for structural variation and an orthogonal-polynomial chaos coordinate for latent stochastic variation.
Use the mean DSS coefficient for energy-based OOD scoring, higher-order coefficients for structured logit variation, and quadrature averaging for the predictive distribution and calibration.
Provide a capacity theorem showing a restricted DSS family can match Gaussian-latent random graph signal chaos coefficients under full-rank features, with controlled truncation error.
evidence_signal: Experiments report the lowest Brier score on 14 node classification benchmarks for DSS-GNN, best AUROC on most node-OOD settings and strongest shifted accuracy on all 7 GOOD concept-shift benchmarks for DSS-Hybrid.
watch_item: The strongest results depend on the chosen deployment mode and empirical evaluation, so task transfer and cross-mode performance can vary and should be validated for a specific graph setting.
paper_title: A Unified Uncertainty Representation for Graph Neural Networks via Doubly-Spectral Stochastic Expansion
